installation.note: rm is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: rm (remove) deletes files and directories permanently. Unlike moving files to trash, rm removes files immediately and they cannot be easily recovered. Use with extreme caution, especially with wildcards or the -r flag. Always verify files before deleting.
when_to_use: Delete files you no longer need

syntax.description: Remove the specified file(s) or directory(ies). Multiple files can be specified. Use -r to remove directories.

misconceptions.title: rm moves files to trash
misconceptions.misconception: rm sends files to a trash/recycle bin like graphical file managers
misconceptions.reality: rm permanently deletes files immediately. They don't go to trash - they're gone. Recovery is difficult and requires special tools.
misconceptions.tip: rm permanently deletes. If you want trash functionality, use a file manager or trash-cli tool.

misconceptions.title: rm can be undone
misconceptions.misconception: Deleted files can be easily recovered
misconceptions.reality: rm deletes files permanently. While recovery is sometimes possible with special tools before filesystem overwrites, it's not guaranteed or easy.
misconceptions.tip: Always be certain before using rm. Consider backups or trash utilities if you want recovery options.

misconceptions.title: rm needs -r for all directories
misconceptions.misconception: rm always requires -r to delete directories
misconceptions.reality: rm -r is required for non-empty directories. Empty directories can be deleted with rm -d or rmdir. Non-empty directories need -r.
misconceptions.tip: Use rm -r for directories with contents, rm -d or rmdir for empty directories

common_pitfalls.description: Accidentally deleting everything including system files
common_pitfalls.solution: NEVER use rm -rf / (will delete entire system). Always double-check paths. Use absolute paths carefully. Consider using -i for safety.
Test wildcards with ls first: ls *.txt to see what matches, then use rm if correct. Use -i for interactive confirmation.

common_pitfalls.description: Trying to delete directory without -r flag
common_pitfalls.solution: Use rm -r for directories. Error will say 'Is a directory' if you forget. Use rmdir for empty directories.

common_pitfalls.description: rm doesn't ask for confirmation by default
common_pitfalls.solution: Use -i for interactive mode to get confirmation prompts. Always verify with ls before deleting.

common_pitfalls.description: Expecting files to be recoverable after rm
common_pitfalls.solution: Assume files are gone forever after rm. Use backups or trash utilities if you need recovery options.

related_commands.relationship: Secure deletion; rm only removes file entries
related_commands.description: Securely delete files by overwriting them before removal

related_commands.relationship: Trash utility; safer alternative to rm

best_practices: ALWAYS use -i (interactive) when deleting important files or using wildcards
Test wildcards with ls first before using with rm
Double-check paths before executing rm, especially with -r or -f
Use -v (verbose) to see what's being deleted
Consider using trash-cli instead of rm for recoverable deletion
NEVER use rm -rf / (will delete entire system)
Use rmdir for empty directories (safer than rm -r)
Verify files exist with ls before deleting
Keep backups of important files before deletion
performance_tips: rm is fast for local file deletions
Deleting many small files may be slower than deleting one large file
rm -rf on large directories may take time
Use rm -f in scripts when you're certain, but test first

additional_notes.permanent_deletion: rm permanently deletes files - they don't go to trash. Recovery is difficult.
additional_notes.recursive_deletion: Use -r or -R for directories. Be very careful with rm -rf - it's powerful but dangerous.
additional_notes.interactive_mode: Always use -i when unsure. Better safe than sorry.
additional_notes.wildcard_danger: Test wildcards with ls first before using with rm
additional_notes.critical_warning: NEVER use rm -rf / or rm -rf * without careful consideration - can cause system-wide data loss
additional_notes.permissions: You need write permission on parent directory to delete files. Use sudo if needed, but be very careful.
additional_notes.alternatives: Consider trash-cli or file manager for safer deletion with recovery options
